risks: Minimal for the evaluation itself, which uses routine records. The pathway change carries the clinical risk of a missed problem, which the balancing measures watch; the evaluation must not delay reporting such problems to the clinical team.
consent: No individual consent is sought for routine records under the service evaluation determination; the optional day 8 questionnaire in 2027 is anonymous and says so, and returning it is voluntary.
data: Extraction by the nurse consultant into a password-protected spreadsheet with a study number instead of name or hospital number; postcodes are converted to distances and then deleted; the file is kept on the service's restricted drive and destroyed two years after the report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: rural patients bear the largest travel costs and gain most from the change, while people with hearing impairment, limited English or no reliable phone signal may be poorly served by a telephone review. In-person day 3 remains available on request, interpreter telephone lines are used for calls, and costs and consequences are reported separately for patients who kept an in-person visit.
effectiveness: The evaluation shows whether the change lowers costs without raising unplanned attendances or infections; it does not claim effects on pain outcomes.
efficiency: Four hours a week of existing staff time and existing records; no new data systems.
costs: Staff time only; the questionnaire is printed in the clinic.
grants: None needed; a positive result could support a regional proposal to extend telephone follow-up after implantation.
partnerships: Pain service manager, finance department, two patient partners from the neuromodulation support group and the emergency department audit lead.
rebPath: Classified by the hospital research office as a service evaluation of routinely collected data (SE-2026-077); no REB submission is required. Any later publication follows CHEERS 2022 and the journal's policy on service evaluations.
limitations: Historical comparison; patient costs estimated rather than measured in 2026; rare consequences are imprecise.
summary: Minimal-risk service evaluation with an in-person option kept for patients poorly served by telephone and equity reporting by that group.
